stances.claim: Calleja v. Executive Secretary (Dec 7, 2021) -- a 235-page Carandang ponencia plus 11 separate opinions totaling 640 pages -- is, IMHO, the most intensely deliberated case in the Gesmundo Court; its facial-challenge ruling upheld the ATA entire except for the Section 4 PROVISO and the second mode of designation in Section 25, leaving as-applied challenges open.

The Court's new ATA Rules (effective Jan 15, 2024) laudably specify 'How' to implement the ATA -- how to tiptoe the terror chasm to preserve constitutional rights, ensure privacy, and defend the presumption of innocence -- recognizing the sui generis nature of terrorism as a crime where prevention matters more than punishment.

The Rules grant CA and RTCs extraordinary ex-parte authority across proscription, surveillance, data preservation, and hold-departure regimes -- a marked departure from our normal adversarial system where judges are passive and rely on 'the rapiers of the contending counsels' -- and this requires magistrates to become 'activists' in scrutinizing documents minutely and examining witnesses personally.

Judicial activism -- far from being a politically loaded concept -- is constitutionally imposed as the solemn duty of our judiciary to strike down grave abuse of discretion, and is a unique and indispensable characteristic of the system of checks and balances in our democracy.
stances.rhetorical_move: doctrinal-rehabilitation of 'judicial activism' as constitutional duty

one_paragraph_summary: In Calleja v. Executive Secretary (Dec 7, 2021), the SC in a 'facial challenge' upheld the constitutionality of the entire Anti-Terrorism Act except for the PROVISO in Section 4 and the 'second mode of designation' in paragraph 2 of Section 25. The 235-page ponencia with 560 footnotes was expertly penned by now-retired Justice Rosmari D. Carandang; together with 11 separate opinions totaling 640 pages -- CJ Gesmundo 199 pages and 762 footnotes (202 more than the ponencia), SAJ Perlas-Bernabe 48, SAJ Leonen 65, Caguioa 130, Lazaro-Javier 41, Inting 21, Zalameda 44, M.V. Lopez 25, Gaerlan 20, J.Y. Lopez 34, Dimaampao 13 -- Calleja is, IMHO, the most intensely deliberated case in the Gesmundo Court. Being a facial determination, the ponencia remains subject to as-applied challenges. Given terrorism's sui generis nature where prevention matters more than punishment, the Court has now promulgated new 'Rules on the Anti-Terrorism Act of 2020 and Related Laws' (effective Jan 15, 2024) that specify 'How' -- how to tiptoe the terror chasm to preserve constitutional rights, ensure privacy, and defend the presumption of innocence. The ATA grants the ATC the power to 'designate' individuals or groups as terrorists and the AMLC the power to issue freeze orders; affected parties may petition the CA to remove their designation on grave-abuse grounds. On SOJ petition, the CA may issue ex-parte within 72 hours, based on probable cause, a Preliminary Order of Proscription to prevent the commission of terrorism, which authorizes AMLC ex-parte preventive freeze orders on terrorism-financing property/funds. After hearing on clear and convincing evidence, the CA may issue a Permanent Order of Proscription effective for three years (shortable/extendable). The CA may also issue ex-parte Surveillance Orders to wiretap with devices and technologies 'now known or subsequently known' and Data Preservation Orders compelling service providers to preserve the surveilled data. The ATA permits warrantless arrest/detention for 14 days, extendable by the proper RTC for 10 more on SOJ verified motion; RTCs may also issue ex-parte Precautionary Hold Departure Orders. These ipso facto powers depart sharply from our normal adversarial system where judges are passive and rely on 'the rapiers of the contending counsels' -- requiring magistrates to be 'activists' in scrutinizing documents minutely and examining witnesses personally. Judicial activism, far from being a politically charged label, is imposed by our Constitution as the solemn duty of our judiciary to strike down grave abuse of discretion -- a unique and indispensable characteristic of the system of checks and balances in our democracy.
